citation: Wadsworth FB et al. (2016), Sintering of viscous droplets under surface tension, Proc R Soc A 472:20150780
license: CC BY 4.0; authors retain copyright; original files copied unchanged, observations.json is a format conversion.
material: Spheriglass A-glass microspheres product 2530, Potters Industries; soda-lime silica. Not clay, sludge or MIA3.

records.source_state: author-processed observations, not raw camera frames
records.repeated_994K_groups: kept as five distinct column groups; no invented specimen IDs or pooling

initial_porosity.locator: main PDF p14 section4b; average across samples, no group-specific values in the data file

initial_pore_radius_m.classification: source-derived from measured particle-size distribution, not an independently measured pore radius

surface_tension_n_m.classification: author-selected dry-silicate literature value, not direct same-sample measurement

vft_2016.classification: explicit interpreted correction of missing logarithm using VFT source; not a publisher erratum

vft_2014.locator: Wadsworth2014 DOI10.1002/2014JB011453 Table2 glass-bead column; coefficients kept together
vft_2014.classification: prior published version sensitivity; viscosity predicted from composition using Fluegel2007, not direct same-sample viscosity observations

equations.vented_radius: supplement EqS5, constant incompressible matrix: da/dt=-Gamma*(a^3+c)/(2*mu*c), c=a_i^3*(1-phi_i)/phi_i
equations.endpoint: finite closure at tau=2*integral_0^1 dx/(1+k*x^3), k=phi_i/(1-phi_i); main text statement of zero only at infinite time is inconsistent with EqS5. Stop the positive-radius domain at closure; no negative-radius continuation.

observational_limits: Supplement Figure3 thermocouple lies within1.5mm of sample base; not an internal sample temperature measurement.
Temperature history is prescribed from each data column and linearly interpolated; nominal header temperature is never substituted for recorded temperature.
Initial recorded823K is near approximately824K glass-transition onset; use of equilibrium VFT viscosity near that onset is conditional.
Main section3c reconstructs porosity using calibrated final volume/porosity; raw silhouettes and group-specific initial porosity are unavailable here.
Printed Error columns are preserved without assigning statistical confidence or complete model uncertainty.
Normalized porosities above1 and fluctuations are kept, not clipped.
Main Eq2.20 nonzero-final-porosity correction explicitly violates strict derivation; not imported into this mechanics benchmark.
Main Figure2 upper temperature axis labelled K is inconsistent with T/Tg and Tg824K. No curve is digitized using that axis.

Supplement Figure3 temperature axis is also labelled K while curves are around568-891, inconsistent with recorded841-1164K by about273K. Use the explicit tabulated K values and preserve the figure-label discrepancy.

Group09 source lines284 and303 contain negative normalized porosity and negative printed Error. Retained unchanged; no physical or confidence-interval interpretation assigned. See observation-quality.json.
scope: Fixed-source-parameter conditional comparison of a vented-pore law with public processed glass observations; no fitted radii, no real-brick qualification, no complete late-stage permeability model.

published_fitted_radius_not_used.locator: main PDF p12 Table1, vented bubble phi->0; section4b(ii) p13
published_fitted_radius_not_used.classification: fit to these experiments; not an independent prediction and not substituted for distribution-derived5.9um. Difference does not alone identify the missing mechanism.

later_primary_vft_confirmation.finding: Explicit log10(mu) and exactly the2016 coefficients with T in Kelvin. Confirms interpretation, not a formal erratum or brick-material property.

findings: Eq2.27 repeats the unnormalized1+zeta polydisperse survival. Three porosities and two source-described mathematical distribution examples fail normalization; the separate Eq2.24 monodisperse survival normalizes.
The text after Eq2.26 prints a=mean(zeta)/mean(R), with inverse-length dimensions despite defining zeta=a/R. Multiplication is the dimensionally consistent identity.

Acquired2016 supplemental time-series do not provide the measured particle moments needed to reproduce the experimental derived mean radius. The benchmark preserves the reported5.9um value without silently correcting it.
